item.title: Treat the patient, not the urine bag?
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody I was interested to read this article which nicely explained the phenomenon of purple urine bags. Guidelines from around the world agree that the presence of bacteria in the urine is inevitable in patients who have long term catheters, and in itself this is not harmful. item.title: Making spiritual care comprehensive
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody This article was refreshingly different from most that deal with spiritual care. For one thing, most previous articles have been grounded on Christian faith, though only about 31% of global population are Christians. Moreover, the article did not compartmentalize different domains of suffering (physical, social, emotional, spiritual) and had a holistic emphasis on personhood and on unconditional care.
